articles.originalTitle: The 90s: Art and Fashion - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Britain Exhibition Explores Art and Fashion of the 1990s
articles.excerpt: Tate Britain presents The 90s: Art and Fashion exhibition, curated with Edward Enninful. The showcase runs from October 8, 2026, to February 14, 2027.
articles.content: Tate Britain has launched The 90s: Art and Fashion exhibition, exploring the creative energy and cultural shifts of the 1990s. Drawing on the experience of curator Edward Enninful OBE, the showcase brings together photography, fashion, art, and design from a generation that transformed British culture. Visitors can encounter works by artists and photographers such as Steve McQueen, Sarah Lucas, Yinka Shonibare, Corinne Day, and Juergen Teller, alongside fashion designs by Vivienne Westwood, Alexander McQueen, and John Galliano. The exhibition runs from October 8, 2026, to February 14, 2027. Highlights include Mark Leckey's video work tracing British dance music culture, a tartan outfit from Vivienne Westwood's 1993 Anglomania collection, and Yinka Shonibare's sculpture referencing colonial trade routes. The display also features Steve McQueen's silent film Bear and Jim Lambie's site-specific floor installation Zobop. Visitors can purchase an optional audio guide for an additional fee.

articles.originalTitle: How an Isle of Wight farm building became an architect’s modern-day retreat - Wallpaper*
articles.title: Historic Farm Building on the Isle of Wight Transformed Into Modern Retreat
articles.excerpt: Studio Weave founder Je Ahn has transformed a modest 158 sq m barn on the Isle of Wight into a pared-down personal retreat. Guided by deep reuse, the project preserves original materials while adapting the agricultural structure for modern habitation.
articles.content: Studio Weave practice founder Je Ahn acquired an existing 158 sq m barn within a working farm near Cowes on the UK's Isle of Wight, transforming it into a pared-down personal retreat. Operating with a limited budget and the unique advantage of being his own client, Ahn approached the redesign with an emphasis on flexibility and comfort. The Studio Weave team preserved much of the 50-plus-year-old original fabric, leaving original materials exposed and repairing them to meet 21st-century habitation standards. The heart of the home features a large open-plan kitchen and living area with expansive windows, leading through a small corridor to three bedrooms. Meticulous detailing and craftwork were completed in collaboration with Mike at Imphouse and his team, while the landscape was produced alongside Tom Massey Studio. Grounded in the concept of deep reuse, the design repurposes materials found on site for both their narrative and practical value. The minimal interventions ensure the agricultural building retains its historical integrity while functioning as a contemporary residential space.

articles.originalTitle: Art Basel announces 272 exhibitors and a reconfigured showfloor for its 2026 Miami Beach edition - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Miami Beach Announces 272 Exhibitors and Reconfigured Layout for 2026
articles.excerpt: Art Basel Miami Beach will bring together 272 exhibitors from over 40 countries for its 2026 edition, featuring a substantially reconfigured showfloor and a more focused gallery lineup.
articles.content: Art Basel Miami Beach will bring together 272 exhibitors from more than 40 countries and territories for its upcoming edition, reaffirming its position as a major commercial moment in the U.S. art market. Taking place at the Miami Beach Convention Center from December 4 to 6, with VIP preview days on December 2 and 3, the fair introduces a substantially reconfigured layout based on feedback from exhibitors and the Selection Committee. The redesigned floor plan occupies approximately 12 percent less floor space, while the main Galleries sector features about 10 percent fewer exhibitors to create a more concentrated setting. The new layout organizes the space around four hospitality plazas instead of five, distributing blue-chip galleries throughout the showfloor to improve navigation and sightlines. The event spans multiple sectors including Galleries, Kabinett, Nova, Positions, and Survey, welcoming more than thirty first-time participating galleries mostly through its project-based sectors. Zero 10 returns with an expanded presentation dedicated to digital art. Public outdoor projects, partner awards, and institutional collaborations will accompany the main exhibition throughout the week.

articles.originalTitle: Guadalupe Maravilla to Stage Installation at St. John the Divine - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Guadalupe Maravilla to Stage Installation at Cathedral of St. John the Divine
articles.excerpt: Creative Time has commissioned artist Guadalupe Maravilla to present his major installation, Consejos de las Estrellas, in the Synod Hall of the Cathedral of St. John the Divine in Morningside Heights, New York.
articles.content: Creative Time has commissioned artist Guadalupe Maravilla to create a major installation in the Synod Hall of the Cathedral of St. John the Divine in New York's Morningside Heights neighborhood. Presented in collaboration with the Clemente Soto Vélez Cultural and Educational Center, Maravilla's Consejos de las Estrellas will be on view from December 17, 2026, to February 7, 2027. The installation is conceived as a sanctuary space for gathering, reflection and respite during the holiday season. The project will bring together nearly 100 sculptures and textile works, alongside Maravilla's traveling school bus-cum-artwork Mariposa Relámpago. Throughout the exhibition, Maravilla will activate the commission through weekly sound baths, exploring the intersections between art and healing. Maravilla stated that the installation will serve as a place to find warmth and belonging when circumstances such as grief, illness or immigration status deepen feelings of absence. St. John the Divine will additionally serve as a site for mutual aid, gathering and redistributing food, clothing and toys in partnership with local community organizations. Laura Bosley, the cathedral's executive director for programming, noted that the project affirms the institution's commitment to community.

articles.originalTitle: Where 60 Years of Master Craftsmanship Meets Modern Luxury Tech - WWD
articles.title: Adrian Jules Combines HandTailored Craftsmanship With Modern Enterprise Technology
articles.excerpt: Established in 1964, Adrian Jules Custom Clothier has developed an enterprise resource planning system to streamline operations in luxury custom clothing.
articles.content: Founded in Rochester, New York, in 1964, Adrian Jules Custom Clothier integrates over 60 years of hand-tailored craftsmanship with enterprise technology. The company developed an internal Enterprise Resource Planning system to track garments from initial order entry through workshop cutting, construction, and accounting. The platform serves as a central hub for private-label tailors and retailers, offering real-time visibility into fabric availability, pricing, and high-resolution visuals from global vendors. Platinum division CEO Alex Roberti emphasized the company's commitment to family-run values and high quality, while operations president Arnie Roberti noted that technology has streamlined pattern introduction and inventory tracking. Additionally, Adrian Jules has expanded its offerings by creating pattern designs specifically adapted to women's body shapes, helping retail partners capture a broader luxury market.

articles.originalTitle: ‘Eventually everything, if you leave it long enough, will fall back into nature’: Michael Landy on the art of disintegration - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Michael Landy Exhibits Future Ruins Series at Sir John Soane's Museum
articles.excerpt: British artist Michael Landy, known for critiquing consumer culture, is launching a new exhibition of drawings and watercolours at London's Sir John Soane's Museum imagining future ruins of notable buildings.
articles.content: British artist Michael Landy is presenting his new exhibition titled Future Ruins at Sir John Soane's Museum in London. Emerging from the Young British Artist generation, Landy became known for his critiques of consumer culture and his 2001 performance Break Down, in which he destroyed all his possessions. The exhibition draws inspiration from an 18th-century watercolour in the museum's collection by Joseph Michael Gandy, which reimagines the Bank of England as a ruin. The series features detailed drawings and watercolours of notable and lesser-known buildings, including the Bank of England, the Soane's Museum, the New York Stock Exchange, Mar-a-Lago, Chatsworth House, Mussolini's Palazzo della Civiltà Italiana, the Landy family home, and an art supply shop. The works range from nostalgic reflections to critiques of hubris. The exhibition also includes a large pencil portrait titled Self Portrait at the Age of 62. Landy notes that themes of decay and destruction have underpinned his practice throughout his career, and the show features one new sculptural work, Broken Column, consisting of overflowing real bins.

articles.originalTitle: Restoration of earthquake-hit palace in Mantua nears completion - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Fourteen-year earthquake restoration of Mantua's Palazzo Ducale nears completion
articles.excerpt: Restoration work at the 35,000-square-meter Palazzo Ducale complex in Mantua, Italy, following the 2012 earthquakes is nearing completion. Director Stefano L'Occaso stated that about 99% of the work is finished.
articles.content: Earthquakes that struck northern Italy's Emilia-Romagna region in 2012 caused significant damage to the historic Palazzo Ducale complex in Mantua. Restoration projects spanning 14 years at the 35,000-square-meter facility, dating from the 13th century and expanded by the Gonzaga dynasty, are now nearing completion. Palazzo Ducale director Stefano L'Occaso stated that about 99% of the work is finished. The Camera Picta room, featuring frescoes by Andrea Mantegna, and the bell tower of the Basilica Palatina di Santa Barbara, both damaged in the earthquakes, were previously repaired. Recently, the southwest tower, the Appartamento Grande di Castello suite, and a stabilized portico bordering the Giardino dei Semplici garden have been restored and opened to the public. Approximately 15 million euros has been spent on earthquake-related repairs. The Sala delle Sigle room, associated with Francesco II Gonzaga and Isabella d’Este, is scheduled to reopen by the end of the year. Additionally, a special exhibition featuring loans from the Louvre and the Kunsthistorisches Museum opens this month.

articles.originalTitle: A Louis Vuitton foundation exhibition, with ten Van Gogh paintings, reveals the extraordinary vision of an early collector - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Fondation Louis Vuitton in Paris exhibits Gustave Fayet's Van Gogh collection
articles.excerpt: The Fondation Louis Vuitton in Paris is hosting a major exhibition featuring Van Gogh paintings acquired by collector Gustave Fayet between 1901 and 1909. The exhibition remains open until March 8, 2027.
articles.content: The Fondation Louis Vuitton in Paris has opened a comprehensive exhibition exploring the story of Modern art pioneer Gustave Fayet. Opening on October 9, the exhibition features ten of the 16 Van Gogh paintings acquired by Fayet between 1901 and 1909. Bernard Arnault, head of the LVMH group, describes Fayet as one of the best kept secrets in the history of Modern art. Spanning four floors of the Frank Gehry-designed building, the exhibition includes more than 600 works by Fayet and other artists. Among Fayet's acquisitions is Public Garden in Arles, which he purchased for 2,000 francs in 1901. The exhibition also highlights Self-portrait with Bandaged Ear and Pipe, painted two weeks after Van Gogh mutilated his ear. Valued at 200,000 francs shortly before Fayet's death in 1924, Public Garden in Arles and other displayed works focus on the artist's Provence and Auvers periods. By 1909, Fayet had become one of the four largest private collectors of Van Gogh's work. Titled Gustave Fayet: Collector - Artist Designer, the exhibition runs until March 8, 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Ten Spiritualist Women Artists to Know - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Ten Spiritualist Women Artists of the 19th and 20th Centuries
articles.excerpt: The 19th-century Spiritualist movement attracted women seeking refuge from a hostile physical realm. Artists like Georgiana Houghton, Anna Mary Howitt, Anna Cassel, and Hilma af Klint channeled messages from the other side, laying early groundwork for abstraction.
articles.content: Emerging in the mid-19th century, the Spiritualist movement provided a conduit for artists seeking to communicate with otherworldly dimensions. As Jennifer Higgie notes, women found solace in the spiritual realm because the physical world restricted their talents. Georgiana Houghton created entirely abstract watercolors and pencil drawings in the 1860s and 1870s while in trances, attributing her work to dead artists and spirits. Although her 1871 solo exhibition of 155 artworks at the New British Gallery was a financial failure, her practice has gained renewed institutional attention in recent decades. Similarly, British medium Anna Mary Howitt produced automatic drawings and spirit illustrations in the 1850s, becoming a founding member of London’s College of Psychic Studies. Anna Cassel collaborated closely with Hilma af Klint as part of The Five, a Spiritualist group of women. Recent scholarship on Cassel's notebooks indicates substantial contributions to af Klint’s fourteen-series cycle, "Paintings for the Temple." Trained at the Royal Academy of the Arts in Stockholm, af Klint created extensive spiritual works that she marked for exhibition only decades after her death. These women used art to record their otherworldly experiences, predating recognized pioneers of abstraction.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | Moldova Pavilion: HYBRIDREAMS – Imagining otherwise in times of crisis - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Moldova Pavilion at Venice Biennale to host roundtable on art during crises
articles.excerpt: The Moldova Pavilion at the Venice Biennale hosts a roundtable discussion examining how wars and current crises alter ways of imagining the future.
articles.content: Marking the Republic of Moldova's official participation in the International Art Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia, a roundtable discussion explores how war and contemporary crises are reshaping future imagination. Organized in collaboration with the European Cultural Foundation and the European Council on Foreign Relations, the event takes place at the Chiesa dei Santi Geremia e Lucia in Venice, home to the Moldova Pavilion. The programme opens with a guided tour of the church led by priest and architect Don Gianmatteo Caputo. The discussion expands from Moldova's geopolitical realities to address the future of Europe, political thought, and artistic responses to conflict. Participants include former Moldovan Foreign Minister Nicu Popescu, European Cultural Foundation Director André Wilkens, and art historian Silvia Eiblmayr. The session is moderated by curator Adelina Luft.

articles.originalTitle: The design story behind the breathtaking Shenzhen Natural History Museum - Wallpaper*
articles.title: China's New Shenzhen Natural History Museum Reflects Regional Biodiversity
articles.excerpt: Situated in the Pearl River Delta, the Shenzhen Natural History Museum features an undulate form inspired by local ecology and a public rooftop park.
articles.content: Established in China's Pingshan District, the Shenzhen Natural History Museum was designed to reflect the region's rich biodiversity. Created by a consortium of 3XN, B+H Architects, and Zhubo Design, the structure encompasses 100000 square metres of exhibition and visitor spaces. Kim Herforth Nielsen from the design team stated that the ambition was to create a piece of landscape shaped by local geology and water. The museum's curvy facade, clad in granite and lamella shingle elements, resembles a cliff emerging from the water. Meanwhile, the entire roof functions as a public park for visitors. Aligned with the ecological systems of Yanzi Hill and the Pingshan River, the project utilized advanced digital models and parametric programmes to coordinate with the topography. David Stavros from B+H Architects noted that the museum makes the city's relationship with nature visible.

articles.originalTitle: ENR 2026 Top 100 Green Design Firms and Contractors: Green Building Market Deepens - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Green Building Market Deepens While Navigating Cost and Policy Challenges
articles.excerpt: While sustainable design and contracting revenues are on the rise, industry stakeholders are grappling with challenges such as federal incentive rollbacks, rising costs, and data gaps.
articles.content: Last year, the revenue of the top 100 green design firms increased by 17.1% to $11.8 billion, while international green design revenue rose 18.3% to $2.15 billion. The revenue of the top 100 green contractors also increased by 5.9% to $101.9 billion. While growth varied across markets, the largest increases were observed in industrial processes, hotels, and health care. However, industry experts point out that the rollback of federal sustainability incentives has created a ripple effect on project costs. Jill Kurtz from Stantec notes that many projects face uncertainties regarding real-world performance, emphasizing that decisions should be grounded in building science and operational data rather than certifications alone. Renée Azerbegi of Mead & Hunt states that shifting policy priorities and reduced incentive programs have generated funding uncertainty. Anica Landreneau from HOK reported that clients are increasingly concerned about grid reliability and energy resilience. Contractors suggest that bringing designers and trade partners together early on is critical in translating sustainability goals into practical decisions.

articles.originalTitle: From Relic to Infrastructure: Can India's Historic Water Systems Work Again? - ArchDaily
articles.title: Can Historic Indian Water Systems Function Again as Modern Urban Infrastructure?
articles.excerpt: Traditional Indian water structures and underground cisterns are being examined for their potential to help modern cities manage water stress. While restorations and research highlight storage capacities, governance and maintenance challenges remain significant.
articles.content: Traditional Indian water architecture is being re-examined as cities face seasonal rainfall and municipal water stress. In Ahmedabad, historical domestic and communal water storage relied on distributed underground cisterns known as Tankas, which collected rainwater from roofs and courtyards into lime-lined chambers. A 2026 study in Built Heritage estimates that roughly 10,000 such structures may still exist beneath domestic courtyards across the city. Although the expansion of centralized municipal supply systems eventually rendered household rainwater structures dormant, their underlying engineering demonstrates how buildings can function as catchment and storage networks. Survey data from the 2026 research indicates that 90 percent of questioned residents are willing to reintegrate Tanka water into the urban system, though barriers concerning governance, ownership, water quality, and maintenance persist. In another case, the restoration of the Bansilalpet stepwell in Hyderabad involved removing 2,000 tonnes of debris to uncover a freshwater source with an estimated water-carrying capacity of 2.2 million liters. Researchers emphasize that reviving these historic structures requires more than masonry repairs; it demands established routines of cleaning, water testing, community involvement, and sustained municipal coordination.

articles.originalTitle: In the Sonoran Desert, a Market Hall–Inspired Library by Richärd Kennedy Architects is Designed for Flexibility - Architectural Record
articles.title: A Market Hall-Inspired Library Designed for Flexibility in the Sonoran Desert
articles.excerpt: Designed by Richärd Kennedy Architects, the Gateway Public Library in Mesa, Arizona, offers a flexible civic hub inspired by traditional market halls. Completed in December 2025, the approximately 28,300-square-foot building addresses local public space needs within a park setting.
articles.content:
Completed in December 2025 in Mesa, Arizona, the Gateway Public Library was designed by Richärd Kennedy Architects to address a shortfall in civic infrastructure and public open space. Spanning approximately 28,270 square feet, the building draws formal cues from traditional market halls, utilizing an overarching structure to connect seamlessly with the surrounding public park rather than acting as a self-contained facility.

The structure features a glazed central gallery with an angular, south-sloping roof supported by slender steel columns and undulant timber planes that dampen noise. Industrial materials such as weathering steel and fiber-cement cladding define the smaller programmatic volumes housed underneath the sprawling canopy. To manage the desert climate, deep roof overhangs provide shade throughout the day, while a variable refrigerant-flow HVAC system is embedded within the floor slab.

Interior finishes include polished concrete flooring and sound-absorbing panels. The smaller volumes, assigned to functions like administration, makerspaces, and children's areas, are built for easy reorganization using floor boxes with data and power placed at regular intervals. Engineering services for the project were provided by Kimley-Horn, with landscape design by Dig Studio and construction by Willmeng Construction.

articles.originalTitle: Members' Tour: The Genius of Renaissance Sculptors: Donatello and Michelangelo - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Hosts Special Tour Exploring Donatello and Michelangelo
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum has announced a guided tour exploring the works of Donatello and Michelangelo led by Boe Paschall. Scheduled for 26 November 2026, tickets for the event are priced at 15 pounds.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum is organizing a members-only guided tour exploring the works of Donatello and Michelangelo within its permanent collection. Led by V&A guide Boe Paschall, the event will take place on Thursday, 26 November 2026, from 15.00 to 16.00 at the V&A South Kensington in the Blavatnik Hall. Tickets are priced at 15.00 pounds and include refreshments following the tour in the Members' Room. The session examines how the technical abilities of both sculptors revolutionized the art form during an era of religious and political upheaval, touching upon the Protestant Reformation, papal extravagance, and controversies surrounding nudity. Organizers note that the tour involves extensive walking and stairs, advising those with accessibility questions to contact the membership team directly. The program offers participants a deeper look into the historical backstories of Renaissance Florence and the profound impact these masters left on sculptural traditions.

articles.originalTitle: Tishman Speyer Buys New York City’s Chrysler Building for Second Time - Architectural Record
articles.title: Tishman Speyer Acquires New York's Chrysler Building Ground Lease Again
articles.excerpt: Tishman Speyer has secured a 150-year ground lease for New York's iconic 77-story Chrysler Building in a $235 million agreement with Cooper Union, including extensive restorations and modernizations.
articles.content: A new chapter begins for the 77-story Chrysler Building in New York City following a newly announced 150-year ground lease agreement between real estate firm Tishman Speyer and land owner The Cooper Union. The $235 million investment encompasses lease payments and the restoration of the landmark situated in Midtown Manhattan. Tishman Speyer previously arranged a similar acquisition and restoration for the tower in 1997. In recent years, the 1.3 million-square-foot skyscraper experienced declining valuations and soaring vacancy rates. Under the new agreement, Tishman Speyer will execute an extensive improvement program. The revitalization will feature the restoration of the historic art deco facade, renewal of the crown, and modernization of mechanical, elevator, and electrical systems. The 61st floor and underground arcade will be transformed into dedicated amenity spaces for fitness, wellness, and gatherings. According to Cooper Union President Steven W. McLaughlin, the agreement integrates into a financial framework that sustains the institution's educational mission. Tishman Speyer CEO Rob Speyer noted that the ambitious plan arrives at a robust moment for the Manhattan office market.

articles.originalTitle: Peggy Guggenheim Exhibition to Be at the Royal Academy - WWD
articles.title: Royal Academy to Host Peggy Guggenheim Exhibition in London
articles.excerpt: London's Royal Academy of Arts is revisiting the history of the Guggenheim Jeune gallery with a new exhibition bringing historic works back to the capital.
articles.content: London's Royal Academy of Arts is revisiting the legacy of the Guggenheim Jeune gallery this fall with Peggy Guggenheim in London: The Making of a Collector. In under a year of operation, Guggenheim Jeune staged more than 20 exhibitions before closing in June 1939. Its historical program included Vasily Kandinsky's first solo show in the United Kingdom, Britain's inaugural collage exhibition, and a dedicated sculpture presentation. The upcoming exhibition features works from the original program, including pieces by Eileen Agar, Salvador Dalí, Barbara Hepworth, Rita Kernn-Larsen, Henry Moore, Piet Mondrian, Cedric Morris, and Sophie Taeuber-Arp. Many of these works are returning to London for the first time since their initial debut. According to the supporting organization, the partnership reflects its roots in Venice alongside a commitment to craftsmanship and creative freedom. The exhibition will run from Nov. 21 through March 14, before traveling to the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum in New York in April.

articles.originalTitle: Downtown Architecture Programs in Calgary and Birmingham Are a Lesson in Urban Renewal - Architectural Record
articles.title: Calgary and Birmingham Projects Turn Vacant Structures Into Architecture Schools
articles.excerpt: Vacant buildings in Calgary and Birmingham have been repurposed to house university architecture programs. Designed by HCMA and Williams Blackstock Architects, these adaptive-reuse projects contribute to local urban revitalization.
articles.content: Two urban adaptive-reuse projects in Calgary, Canada, and Birmingham, Alabama, demonstrate how vacant downtown structures can be successfully converted into architecture schools. In Calgary, HCMA Architecture + Design transformed the lower floors of a 1982 office tower into a new home for the University of Calgary's School of Architecture, Planning and Landscape. The 180,000-square-foot complex, completed at a cost of roughly $22 million, accommodates up to 1,200 students within a vertical campus setting. Meanwhile, in Birmingham, Williams Blackstock Architects adapted a six-story 1914 former furniture showroom into a satellite facility known as Auburn in Birmingham, primarily housing the Urban Studio and a design lab. This $17.5 million project involved terra-cotta facade restoration and cutting floor plates to introduce natural light deeper into the 44,000-square-foot building. Both educational spaces deliberately expose raw structural elements, such as concrete cores, original columns, and construction markings, to serve as pedagogical tools for students. These interventions aim to revitalize struggling urban cores by integrating academic programs directly into city centers.

articles.originalTitle: Cosima von Bonin’s soft toys storm the Petit Palais - Art Basel
articles.title: Cosima von Bonin Unveils Dollys & Beaux Exhibition at Petit Palais
articles.excerpt: German artist Cosima von Bonin presents the Dollys & Beaux exhibition at the Petit Palais for Art Basel Paris's public program, bringing together her fabric sculptures and soft toy figures.
articles.content: Kenyan-born German artist Cosima von Bonin is presenting the Dollys & Beaux exhibition at the Petit Palais as part of Art Basel Paris's public program. The exhibition features large-scale soft-stuffed leather, velvet, and mohair sculptures created by the artist. These figures, which previously appeared in Loewe's Fall/Winter 2026 collection show, establish a dialogue between contemporary art and fashion. The presented works include velvet St. Bernard dog sculptures with plush barrels around their necks, sea scallops, a hermit crab, an octopus, and a killer whale. Spanning a career of over 40 years, von Bonin's installations encourage open-ended interpretations from viewers rather than imposing a single narrative. Miu Miu serves as the official partner for the public program. Dollys & Beaux is on view at the Petit Palais from October 23 to 25, 2026, while Art Basel Paris takes place at the Grand Palais from October 23 to 25, 2026.

articles.originalTitle: In Transit with artist Nour Jaouda - Art Basel
articles.title: Exploring Space, Memory, and Movement with Artist Nour Jaouda
articles.excerpt: In an interview as part of the In Transit series produced in partnership with Qatar Airways, Libyan artist Nour Jaouda discusses how travel, memory, and cultural mobility shape her textile and sculptural practices.
articles.content: Working with sculptural, hand-dyed textiles and hanging fiber installations, Libyan artist Nour Jaouda explores how spaces embody memory. Based between Cairo and London, Jaouda notes that moving between diverse social and cultural landscapes has informed her visual language. A 2023 visit to Benghazi, where she reconnected with a decades-old fig tree in her grandmother's garden, directly influenced her tapestries created for the 2024 Venice Biennale. Explaining that carrying a prayer mat during travels grounds her, she emphasizes the importance of this ritual. Connecting color to movement, Jaouda employs deconstruction and décollage techniques to create meaning through unmaking and restructuring. In Cairo, she finds inspiration in the architectural layers of Downtown, while in London, she prefers walking aimlessly to discover subtle moments. At Art Basel Qatar, her installation A House Between Two Houses presented a space shaped by emotional subjectivity and memory rather than fixed geography, engaging with concepts of transformation and decay. Watching the fair come to life in Doha and meeting fellow creators provided her with an insightful experience rooted in a rich history.

articles.originalTitle: Yohji Yamamoto Drawings - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Hosts Talk on Unpublished Yohji Yamamoto Drawings
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum will host an event celebrating a collection of previously unpublished drawings by designer Yohji Yamamoto.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting a special talk and book celebration on Wednesday 9 December to mark the publication of Yohji Yamamoto Drawings. Author and curator Alexandre Samson will join Yohji Yamamoto's executive advisor, Caroline Fabre, at V&A South Kensington to discuss a collection of never-before-published drawings selected by Yamamoto himself. Featuring menswear and womenswear sketches designed with support from Peter Saville, the book offers insight into the designer's creative process and his exploration of fashion and form. Samson and Fabre will discuss Yamamoto's creative practice and the enduring legacy of his work during the evening event, which includes a wine reception and book signing. Priority booking for members is open, with general ticket sales beginning on 19 October, subject to availability. Ticket prices range from 15.00 to 20.00 pounds and include the post-talk reception.

articles.originalTitle: Painting large as an Impressionist: Renoir and the full-length format | Events - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: National Gallery Examines Renoir and Full-Length Portraiture
articles.excerpt: Colin B. Bailey, Director of The Morgan Library and Museum, will deliver a special lecture at the National Gallery's Pigott Theatre exploring Pierre-Auguste Renoir's large-scale portraits.
articles.content: The National Gallery is hosting a special event focusing on Pierre-Auguste Renoir's full-length portraits, recognized among the most ambitious works of his career. Held in conjunction with the exhibition Renoir and Love, the lecture features Colin B. Bailey, Katharine J. Rayner Director of The Morgan Library & Museum, who will examine how the artist captured modern life, emotions, and social interactions in 19th-century Paris. Drawing on decades of research into eighteenth- and nineteenth-century French art, Bailey will explore Renoir's technical brilliance, evolving portraiture approach, and psychological immediacy. The talk will take place in the Pigott Theatre on Level -1 of the Sainsbury Wing. Standard tickets are priced at 10 pounds, while concessions are available at 8 pounds for full-time students, jobseekers, and disabled adults. Advance booking is required for attendance, and members will have the option to join the event online. This lecture offers audiences a distinct opportunity to closely examine the artist's celebrated figures within the broader context of friendship, love, and modernity explored throughout the exhibition.

articles.originalTitle: Renoir and Love | Exhibitions - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: National Gallery in London Opens Major Renoir and Love Exhibition
articles.excerpt: The National Gallery in London presents Renoir and Love, an exhibition exploring the artist's depiction of human connections and everyday emotions through 40 paintings gathered from international collections, on view until January 31, 2027.
articles.content: The National Gallery in London presents Renoir and Love, an exhibition focusing on Pierre-Auguste Renoir's exploration of love, friendship, and human connection during his peak period from the 1860s to the 1880s. Running until January 31, 2027, the exhibition brings together 40 paintings from collections across the world, highlighting the artist's role as an innovator of Impressionism. Notably, Renoir's iconic 1876 painting Bal au Moulin de la Galette from the Musée d'Orsay is on display in the United Kingdom for the first time. The exhibition is organized jointly by the Musée d'Orsay, the National Gallery, and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. Visitors can explore sun-dappled gardens, dance halls, and intimate everyday moments captured by the artist, with flexible pay-what-you-wish admission options available on select Friday evenings.

articles.originalTitle: Roy Lichtenstein: Like New | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Roy Lichtenstein Retrospective Opens at Whitney Museum in New York
articles.excerpt: The Whitney Museum of American Art presents Roy Lichtenstein: Like New, marking the artist's first retrospective in New York since 1993 and gathering roughly 130 works created from the early 1940s through the 1990s.
articles.content: The Whitney Museum of American Art in New York hosts Roy Lichtenstein: Like New from October 11, 2026, to May 10, 2027. Marking the artist's first major retrospective in the city since 1993, the exhibition traces how Lichtenstein's early interest in perception and visual recognition shaped a career-long investigation into duplication, simulation, and image culture. Featuring approximately 130 works produced from the early 1940s to the 1990s, the exhibition explores his treatment of images as unstable forms subject to borrowing, translation, and reframing. For the first time, all works from Lichtenstein's inaugural Pop-style exhibition at the Leo Castelli Gallery in 1962 are reunited. This pivotal moment defined an era and extended its impact beyond Pop art, shaping subsequent generations of artists whose works are also displayed within the exhibition.

articles.originalTitle: Patek Philippe Unveils Seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan, Debuts Limited-edition Timepieces - WWD
articles.title: Patek Philippe Unveils Seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan
articles.excerpt: Patek Philippe launched its seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition at CityOval Milano, showcasing historic timepieces alongside new limited-edition models.
articles.content: Swiss watchmaker Patek Philippe opened the seventh and largest edition of its Watch Art Grand Exhibition at CityOval Milano, formerly known as Palazzo delle Scintille. Spanning 31,215 square feet, the exhibition features over 500 watches and clocks from the brand's history and museum collections. Patek Philippe president Thierry Stern noted the longstanding importance of the Italian market during a preview walk-through. The exhibition runs through October 18 and includes 25 pieces inspired by Italian landscape and culture, alongside seven new limited-edition references featuring the inscription Patek Philippe Milano 2026 on the sapphire crystal caseback. Among the new introductions are three Calatrava iterations with red, white, and green lacquered dials, as well as the debut of the Gondolo Ladies First jewelry collection. The exhibition coincides with Milano Watch Week at Palazzo Mezzanotte.

articles.originalTitle: TfL reveals civil engineering behind £15.3M step-free upgrades at Surrey Quays and Northolt - New Civil Engineer
articles.title: Step-Free Access Completed at Surrey Quays and Northolt Stations in London
articles.excerpt: Transport for London details completed step-free access projects at Surrey Quays and Northolt stations, delivered through a total investment of £15.3M.
articles.content: Surrey Quays and Northolt railway stations in London have been upgraded to provide step-free access for wheelchair users, parents with pushchairs, and travellers with luggage. According to Transport for London (TfL), the improvements at Surrey Quays were supported by funding from the Housing Infrastructure Fund programme alongside a contribution from British Land. Lead designer AtkinsRéalis and contractor Morgan Sindall Infrastructure minimized the carbon footprint by utilizing low-carbon cement and electric arc furnace steel. The concourse building also features a green roof and solar panels. The upgrade works at Northolt station were funded by TfL at an estimated cost of £15.3M, introducing a new footbridge and lift to establish step-free connections between the street and trains. Stuart Harvey, TfL chief capital officer, stated that the completed projects will significantly improve journeys for thousands of customers across the network.
